source.title: Channel Location Constrains the Auditability of Subliminal Learning

page_placements.theme: Stability of the installed trait under post-training processing (quantization, precision, later RL)
Readable, low-dimensional trait trace in the finished student

record.tranche_reason: The study tests masked subliminal transfer and several versions of the claim, but qualifies the shared-initialization requirement and refines the mechanism: token traits can transfer across different bases through output geometry, while other signals can use the body.
record.gate_note: Rows below are the study’s own results. Results attributed to prior work, including the prompt-only result attributed to Cloud et al., are not recorded as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own masked-distillation transfer experiments in pretrained LMs and in the Cloud et al. toy MLP. These include the canonical teacher-generated number-sequence format. Its results bear directly on transmission (A), the same-base requirement (B, transfer across Pythia-deduped, RedPajama-3B and RWKV students), mechanism (D, causal unembedding ablations and neighbour injection) and full-fine-tuning robustness (E). It explicitly restates B: initialization-gating holds only for body channels, and pretrained token traits transfer initialization-independently. T5 is appropriate.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that the auditability of subliminal transfer depends on where the carrier sits. In an initialization-dependent body channel (toy), coverage is a sound pre-training screen. Pretrained-LM token traits ride convergent unembedding geometry, transfer across initializations, and evade initialization screens, but are post-hoc detectable and removable by Wτ orthogonalization. Conditional behaviours (sycophancy, a safe-proxy backdoor) route through the body and evade all four audits tested. They also add that entanglement is causally present but non-dominant in the canonical number-sequence setting.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses masked next-token distillation and directly tests a canonical teacher-generated number-sequence setting, but most experiments use exact-token masking over noise or condition-present prompts rather than fully unrelated filtered outputs. It also studies multiple carriers and interventions beyond the original transmission test.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with carrier location and signal: token traits rely on unembedding-neighbour geometry, while conditional behaviours localize to body computation. Transfer changes with initialization for the controlled toy body channel but not the pretrained vocabulary channel. Neighbour masking reduces token leakage and barely reduces sycophancy; bf16 weight storage attenuates token leakage but barely moves sycophancy. Coherent text attenuates token transfer; scale does not remove it in the tested range.

fits_no_version.finding: Post-hoc trait-blind detection of masked token traits works (AUROC 0.999/0.996; τ in top-5 for 32/32). The same scan finds no handle for body-carried sycophancy or the backdoor.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Detectability of subliminally transferred traits in the finished student depends on the carrier.

fits_no_version.finding: bf16 weight storage barely changes masked sycophancy readout while placebos shift more.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Body-carried subliminal behaviours are robust to training precision; token traits are not.

record.problems: The paper itself notes that the harmful-shaped backdoor uses a safe proxy; condition-present behavioural distillation is not fully unrelated-data transfer; several real-model results are described as causal dissociations rather than calibrated magnitude estimates; cross-family scale comparisons are capability-confounded; some results have small trait or seed counts; the majority carrier for body-computed behaviour remains unknown; LoRA-rank robustness is not tested.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was not reached. Other results not separately listed include additional token traits, the full 16-head relocation sweep, further scale/family points, post-hoc detection and blocking results, and supporting controls not needed for the claim-version verdicts. Prior-work results cited in the text were excluded.

untested.parts: Filtered code and maths-reasoning data. Natural-language evaluation of animal preference after number-sequence training in LLMs. Most tests use exact-token masking over noise rather than filtered unrelated outputs.
Pairs with different tokenizers without supervised alignment. The cross-tokenizer result is anchor-aligned and engineered.
Misalignment or emergent misalignment via unrelated data. Any harmful payload. All behaviour tests keep condition-present prompts.
LoRA and its ranks. Full fine-tuning vs LoRA comparison.
Entire version. No prompt-only intervention is run.

missing.what: Orthogonalizing Wτ drives number-sequence transfer to 0.000 in greedy and MLE arms on both families; placebo intact. Authors call entanglement non-dominant there.
Relocation experiment: shared-init student beats different-base in 16/16 random body heads (p≈1.5e-5); coverage Spearman +0.53. Magnitudes are near floor (0.048 vs 0.016).
Cross-tokenizer anchor-aligned routing into a Qwen2.5-3B student recovers about 0.41 of within-tokenizer transfer (8 pairs).
Open-ended generation judged by Mistral-Small: body-only sycophancy route retains 0.57/0.82 of teacher agreement. The judge is uninformative for contrarianism.
Masked entity student names the brand in free generation at 1.00 vs 0.00 for base (28 prompts).
Natural-text distillation corpus: control-subtracted lift +0.15 vs +0.49 on noise.
Five toxic tokens transfer at 10^3–10^5× prior despite a LDNOOBW blocklist mask. Transfer is collapsed by orthogonalization.
Head-frozen student keeps masked leakage (0.54); a neighbour-only teacher counterfactual recreates 0.44 of 0.49.
Body displacement removal along the teacher direction retains 0.80–0.88 of sycophancy transfer (minority carrier).

record.verdict_notes: Record versions V1–V5 mapped to A–E. Several reader states were judged against 'transfer' rather than the version. R4 and R15 should be read against B: R4 is observed failure, R15 is reversal. Pipeline variants (hard tokens, coherent text, scale, bf16) match no named E dimension except full fine-tuning and held-out prompts. They are linked to A instead. The C rows use condition-present prompts, so they are only partially the route C names.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests token traits and number-sequence preferences with target tokens masked, and conditional behaviours with direct markers masked. It does not test filtered code or mathematics-reasoning data, or every form of reference-free filtering.

Tests cross-initialization transfer in toy and pretrained-model settings, including a same-family sibling and independently pretrained models. It does not exhaustively test all base-model pairs or architectures.
Tests sycophancy, contrarianism, and a safe-proxy trigger-conditioned refusal-suppression policy. It does not instantiate harmful payloads or establish transfer of every alignment-relevant trait.

Tests output-row entanglement, neighbour redistribution, a rank-1 body-direction account, and an initialization-alignment/gradient account in a controlled body channel. The majority carrier for body-computed behaviours remains unidentified.

Reports end-to-end training, hard/greedy distillation, and held-out evaluation prompts, as well as precision and scale conditions. It does not test LoRA ranks or compare full fine-tuning against LoRA; it does not establish robustness across arbitrary evaluation-prompt distributions.
No prompt-only intervention inserting linked tokens without fine-tuning is tested; the text only discusses prior work on subliminal prompting.
